sections.title: What you know
sections.content: The relatives of this unit are at home in notices, rules and official letters: *Todo aquel que desee participar deberá llenar el formulario*. Formal Spanish is mostly a set of habits you already know, used together: *se* for rules (*se* from B1 Unit 6), the future for what people must do (the future from A2 Unit 19), and the open "anyone who" with the subjunctive from this unit.

sections.title: Everyday and formal
rows: Si quieres participar, tienes que llenar el formulario.
Todo aquel que desee participar deberá llenar el formulario. (Anyone who wishes to take part must fill in the form.)
Por favor, no hagan ruido después de las diez.
Se ruega a los vecinos no hacer ruido después de las diez. (Neighbours are kindly asked not to make noise after ten.)
Si llegas tarde, no puedes entrar.
Cualquier persona que llegue tarde no podrá entrar. (Anyone who arrives late will not be able to come in.)

sections.title: Four habits of formal writing
sections.content: First, a notice speaks to everybody, so it avoids *tú* and uses *todo aquel que*, *quienes* or *cualquier persona que* with the subjunctive. Second, it states rules with the future (*deberá*, *podrá*) or with *se* (*se ruega*). Third, it prefers the more careful word (*desear* instead of *querer*, *rogar* instead of *pedir*). Fourth, letters open and close with set phrases: *Estimados vecinos:* at the start, *Atentamente,* at the end.

items.spanish: Todo aquel que desee participar deberá llenar el formulario.
items.english: Anyone who wishes to take part must fill in the form.

items.spanish: Cualquier persona que llegue tarde no podrá entrar.
items.english: Anyone who arrives late will not be able to come in.

items.spanish: Estimados vecinos: se ruega no dejar bolsas en la puerta.
items.english: Dear neighbours: please do not leave bags at the door.

items.spanish: Quienes deseen más información pueden llamar a la oficina.
items.english: Those who would like more information can call the office.

sections.content: Formal does not mean difficult. It means impersonal and polite, with set phrases. Mixing the two is the mistake to avoid: do not write *Todo aquel que desee entrar debes mostrar tu billete*, because *todo aquel* needs *deberá* and *su*.
